items.desc: claim.py publishes another worker's staged files: 'git commit' has no pathspec, so it commits the whole index
items.evidence: FOUND by checker 2026-11-23T17:55Z while probing S-63 at 9e61b59. scripts/claim.py does 'git add build-ledger.json && git commit -q -m "claim <id> by <worker>" && git push'. git commit without a pathspec commits EVERYTHING in the index, not just the file that was added — so if any worker has staged-but-uncommitted files in the shared clone, the claim commit sweeps them up and pushes them to origin under the message 'claim <id> by <worker>'. REPRODUCED in an isolated clone (bare origin + shared clone + real claim.py): staged agent_wip.ts carrying WORKER-WIP-MARKER, then claim.py -> exit 0, origin HEAD 'claim X-01 by probe-worker' contains agent_wip.ts (+1) alongside build-ledger.json; 'git grep WORKER-WIP-MARKER HEAD' = hit. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by the S-63 rework: the parent 756f5de has the identical add/commit lines. Not destructive (content is preserved and stays in the tree) but it publishes unreviewed WIP to main and mislabels it under another worker's claim. FIX: pathspec-limit the commit, e.g. git commit -q -m "..." -- build-ledger.json (and keep the soft-reset rollback on the failure path).
